text_en: But you, our God, are kind and true, patient, and ruling all things in mercy.
text_cn: 至于你，我们的天主，你是良善的，忠实的，宽容的，以慈爱治理万有。

text_en: For even if we sin we are yours, knowing your power; but we will not sin, because we know that you acknowledge us as yours.
text_cn: 我们即使犯了罪，仍是你的，因为我们承认你的主权；我们既承认我们原属于你，我们就不再犯罪了。

text_en: For to know you is complete righteousness, and to know your power is the root of immortality.
text_cn: 实在，认识你就是完美的正义；承认你的主权，就是不死不灭的根源。

text_en: For neither has the evil intent of human art misled us, nor the fruitless toil of painters, a figure stained with varied colors,
text_cn: 为此，人邪恶的创作，画家无益的作品，各式各色的画图，都没有使我们误入迷途；

text_en: whose appearance arouses yearning in fools, so that they desire the lifeless form of a dead image.
text_cn: 不过，愚人一见这些画像，就大动情欲，贪恋这些无灵的死像。

text_en: Lovers of evil things and fit for such objects of hope are those who either make or desire or worship them.
text_cn: 凡制造、爱慕、恭敬偶像的，实是邪恶的情人，只堪将希望寄于无灵之物。

text_en: A potter kneads the soft earth and laboriously molds each vessel for our service, fashioning out of the same clay both the vessels that serve clean uses and those for contrary uses, making all alike; but which shall be the use of each of them the worker in clay decides.
text_cn: 有个陶人用力抟（tuán）软泥，制成各种器皿，以供我们使用；但是，他可用同样的泥土，做成为洁净事用的器皿，同样，也可做成为卑污事用的器皿；至于，每件作何用途，皆由陶人断定。

text_en: With misspent toil, these workers form a futile god from the same clay— these mortals who were made of earth a short time before and after a little while go to the earth from which all mortals are taken, when the time comes to return the souls that were borrowed.
text_cn: 后来，他竟枉费心机，将同样的泥土，揑成一个虚无的神像，不想自己不久以前，原是由土造成的；不久以后，天主向他索还灵魂时，还要归于土。

text_en: But the workers are not concerned that mortals are destined to die or that their life is brief, but they compete with workers in gold and silver, and imitate workers in copper; and they count it a glorious thing to mold counterfeit gods.
text_cn: 他并不想死亡将至，生命短促，只图与金匠银匠竞争，仿效铜匠，以制造虚伪之物为荣。

text_en: Their heart is ashes, their hope is cheaper than dirt, and their lives are of less worth than clay,
text_cn: 他的心已如死灰，他的希望比尘埃还卑微，他的生命比泥土更卑贱。

text_en: because they failed to know the one who formed them and inspired them with active souls and breathed a living spirit into them.
text_cn: 因为，他竟不知是谁创造了他，是谁赋给了他一个行动的灵魂，是谁向他吹了生命的气息。

text_en: But they considered our existence an idle game, and life a festival held for profit, for they say one must get money however one can, even by base means.
text_cn: 他反将我们的生命视为儿戏，将此生看作惟利是图的市场，说：“人必须用各样的方法，甚至利用不义的手段，获得利润。”

text_en: For these persons, more than all others, know that they sin when they make from earthy matter fragile vessels and carved images.
text_cn: 凡用泥料制造易破的器皿和偶像的，应比其他一切人更清楚知道自己犯了罪。

text_en: But most foolish, and more miserable than an infant, are all the enemies who oppressed your people.
text_cn: 但是，最愚蠢，比婴儿还可怜的，还是那些仇视并虐待你百姓的人。

text_en: For they thought that all their heathen idols were gods, though these have neither the use of their eyes to see with, nor nostrils with which to draw breath, nor ears with which to hear, nor fingers to feel with, and their feet are of no use for walking.
text_cn: 他们将异邦人所有的偶像都看作神明；这些神明有眼不能看，有鼻不能喘气，有耳不能听，有手不能摸，有脚不能行，

text_en: For a human being made them, and one whose spirit is borrowed formed them; for none can form gods that are like themselves.
text_cn: 因为都是人的作品，是那由天主借得气息的人所捏造的，实在没有一人能造出一个与自己相似的神；

text_en: People are mortal, and what they make with lawless hands is dead; for they are better than the objects they worship, since they have life, but the idols never had.
text_cn: 有死的人，只能用邪恶的手造出死像，他本人原胜过他所崇拜的东西，因为他尚有生命，这些东西却从来没有。

text_en: Moreover, they worship even the most hateful animals, which are worse than all others when judged by their lack of intelligence;
text_cn: 此外，他们竟然还敬拜那些最可憎恶的动物，因为，这些动物与其他动物相比，更为愚笨。

text_en: and even as animals they are not so beautiful in appearance that one would desire them, but they have escaped both the praise of God and his blessing.
text_cn: 再就其为动物而言，也并不美丽，或值得人爱，只是些不得天主赞赏和祝福的东西。
